key_insight: Human and LLM recipe generation can achieve comparable synthesis success, and their closed-loop collaboration helped discover a new material prototype, Ba3PtO5.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests LLMs can accelerate materials synthesis planning when paired with experimental validation, making them useful for exploring complex phase spaces.
method: Generated synthesis recipes for known and unknown Ruddlesden-Popper materials using both humans and LLMs.
Tested recipes in the lab and fed results back into a closed-loop human/LLM workflow.
Compared success rates across two rounds to measure collaboration effects.
evidence_signal: Success rates were similar for humans and LLMs on known materials in round one and two, but much lower on unknown targets; the collaboration still enabled discovery of Ba3PtO5.
watch_item: Results are limited to a well-studied Ruddlesden-Popper materials space, so performance may not transfer to harder or less structured synthesis problems.
paper_title: Human and LLM Collaboration for Accelerated Materials Synthesis and Discovery
